title: I made an online team card game as a solo dev with AI art and audio: Recraft and image editing for the art, ElevenLabs for the music. What worked and what didn't
author: cuky144
selftext:
**Quillsworn** is a turn-based PvP card game: eight classes, 1v1 to 3v3, and your whole team plays its turn at the same time. It's in a free public playtest now (Windows + Linux): [https://norefundsstudio.itch.io/quillsworn](https://norefundsstudio.itch.io/quillsworn). Trailer: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lsea3wGdFoo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lsea3wGdFoo)

I did the design and made every call on what goes in; the art and the audio are AI-made. Here's how that went.

**Art (Recraft, image editing)**

* All 180 card pictures: one generation each from a fixed style block plus one subject line per card. No cherry picking. A consistent prompt mattered more than picking the best of four.
* Heroes were the hard part. Generated on their own, they came out in eight different styles. What worked: generate one hero I liked, then **repaint every other hero with that one as the style reference** (image editing with two images), then remove the background.
* Custom "styles" trained on my own pictures failed: they carried the reference palette, so every class came out in the same colours.
* Small things that saved a lot of time: ask for **no ground shadow** from the start (the game draws its own, and a painted one can't move with an animated figure). Check cut-outs for lost glowing bits like flames and sparks. A few small Python scripts cleaned up halos and stray pixels after background removal.
* The battlegrounds were 16:9 and the game supports 21:9. I padded the sides and inpainted the missing parts, then laid the full-resolution original back over the middle.

**Audio (ElevenLabs)**

* All the music and most sound effects. I generated a few takes of each and picked by ear in the game, not in isolation: a sound that's great on its own can be too much after the 50th card.

**Trailer**

* Recorded with Godot's Movie Maker mode from bot matches, then cut by a script (Python + ffmpeg) that syncs shots to the music's beat. Re-cutting it after adding two classes was a re-run, not a re-edit.

**What I'd do differently**: lock the art style with one reference image on day one, before generating anything else.

Happy to go deeper on any of it. And if you try the game, I'd love to hear how it plays: [https://discord.gg/V4ysgFUrj3](https://discord.gg/V4ysgFUrj3)

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body: Please consider presenting the game with a proper showcase video, not a slideshow gif. You won't attract many viewer if the first thing they see is 1 FPS footage.

replies.author: cuky144
replies.body:
Thanks for the advice! I can’t edit this post, and I’m not sure about deleting it and re-posting it with the video showcase. However, the description has a link to the proper trailer on YouTube.  
Next time I make a post, I’ll keep that in mind.
